image_prompt.text: Waist-high and full-body cover spread evenly down every lane of the match map
Two team bases at opposite ends of the map, shielded from each other's firing lines
Narrow pinch points where the lanes meet, concentrating the gunfights onto contested ground
A practice arena firing line with plate, silhouette and bullseye targets set at graded distances downrange
A weapon rack behind the practice firing line holding the unlockable guns, so players can pick and swap what they are practising with
A lobby sized for a crowd of players waiting to be matched into a game
Portals out of the lobby to the practice arena and to each game mode's map

Static and popping targets in the practice arena, placed so the player can read which distance they are hitting
A weapon bench in the practice arena where players swap between the guns they have unlocked
Paired transport from the lobby to the practice arena and to each game mode's map

skill_gap.name: no multi-map decomposition
skill_gap.why: The prompt asks for a lobby, a practice arena and several game-mode maps. The handoff holds exactly one shape, one option set and one scale band, so three or more places with different shapes and different sizes have to be flattened into one build with a P4 flag on it. Nothing in the emit format can say how many maps there are or which options belong to which.

notes_for_us: options.md gives only 'ID | Concept', not the '**Type (Flavor Name)**' form, so an option taken from the catalogue has no Shared Vocabulary term to fill layout_placement.type. teleporter-link's type was guessed as 'Teleporter'.
teleporter-link is marked *varies* and options.md says to read the note in Build.md before picking a route, but Build.md is out of read scope for this run, so the P4-vs-P0 call was made without it.

preset is a single string, but this prompt needs Team Deathmatch for the match maps and Aim Trainer for the practice arena. The skill sanctions borrowing a second preset's options and then gives nowhere to name it.
count attaches to a pick, so 'about 15 different weapons' only survived because station-loadout happened to be picked. A weapons number on a prompt with no bench in it would be lost entirely.

Step 4 says P4 is not ready and to prefer P0/P6, and also says a plainly stated feature requires its modifier. A prompt that names a lobby, a practice arena and several gamemodes satisfies both readings, and the skill does not say which wins.
